doc.title: Ann Rabson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 21, 2007

title: Listening to Ruth Brown and the blurred lines of genre
summary: She remembers Ruth Brown as wonderful and talkative, and says good music can't be categorized.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis

blocks.x: Miss Rhythm. She’s wonderful. She was a wonderful person too. She was great. I hope that somebody had a tape recorder and talked to her. Because you couldn’t shut her up.
We did an interview with her.
You did an interview with her?
Did she tell you all the dirt on everybody and everything?
She did not. Not to my memory. It was really early on when we did it.

She was everywhere, she knew everyone, she knew all the — I mean I’m not saying she talked bad about people but oh she had such wonderful memories. Yeah she was a wonderful — we lost her this year. We lost a lot of people. But yeah, she was on that juke box and she was a great singer.
And crossed a lot of genres.

Absolutely. jazz, blues, soul. I don’t even know if they had soul at that time. But we used to call — well they used to call it rhythm & blues, rock & roll, and now the rhythm & blues is something completely different now, right?
But yeah. Well she was — really good music to my mind, you can’t categorize it. I mean really. Hank Williams? Is that Country? Well I don’t know. You talk about blues, I mean. Yeah. Ruth Brown.
